scenes.headline: Governance for teams
scenes.sub: Make it safe. Then make it stick.
lines: Lesson eight. Governance.
Your instructor is Patrick Diamitani.
How to roll agents out to a team, safely.

scenes.headline: Rules for agents. Rules for people.
lines: Governance needs two sets of rules.
Rules for the agents, written in their context files.
And rules for the people, written down where everyone can see them.

scenes.headline: Decide what goes where.
lines: Start with data.
Decide what never goes in a prompt.
Which tools the agents may connect to.
And who approves anything new.

scenes.headline: Ask before writing.
lines: Then permissions.
Allow list the safe commands, so it can move fast on the boring stuff.
Deny anything sensitive, like your secrets file.
Everything else, the agent asks first. And keep a log of what it changed.

scenes.headline: Start small. Share everything.
lines: Finally, roll out in steps.
Pilot with one team for thirty days.
Share a skills library in git.
Review it every month, and keep what works.

scenes.headline: What you just learned.
lines: Quick recap.
Two rulebooks, least access, ask-before-write, and a small pilot.
Your mission: write a one page AI playbook for your team, and pick the pilot group.

takeaways.t: Rules for agents and for people
Allow the safe, deny the sensitive

mission.t: Write a one-page AI playbook for your team — and pick the pilot group.

lines: That's the core course.
